root: ^Thelma: Your help was a godsend... I can see now how foolish I was to wander that wharf alone.
^Those thieves were coming for me. If you hadn’t shown up, I’d be lost to some strange land by now...
^forced to betray these sacred trees and shatter the ancient vow I made to the forest.
^You shouldn’t scare your sister like that.
^Why did those thieves want you so badly?

c-0: ^Thelma: Oh, I’ll be fine. Frankly, just another embarassing story to tell at the campsite.
^I’ll rise from this — stronger, sharper. I managed to snag some gold from those cutthroats.
^I’ll use it to level up at the bonfire. No way I’m letting anyone catch me off guard again.
c-1: ^Thelma: Yeah... I know. She already bears enough—taking care of the camp, protecting all of us.
^I hate being a burden. You’ve given me a lot to think about. I want to be better...
^for her, for all of us. She’s the backbone of this place, and I owe her so much more than I give.
c-2: ^Thelma: (sighs, voice low) You’ve earned the truth...
^They’re after my gift—the rare ability to scent the oak trees rich with that magical resin.
^The resin used in elemental coatings for weapons...
^and alchemy far beyond that. It’s a treasure more valuable than gold to the wrong hands.
^Thelma: Those fiends were probably hoping to sell me off to ruthless lumberjacks or alchemists hungry for power. But thanks to you, their scheme crumbled like ash in the wind.
